sources.title: J. Sbierski, On the Existence of a Maximal Cauchy Development for the Einstein Equations - a Dezornification, arXiv:1309.7591v3 (2015), 24 printed pages
sources.locator: Section 2 (Definitions 2.1-2.2, Remark 2.5, Theorems 2.6-2.8) and Section 3 (Lemmas 3.1, 3.3, 3.8, 3.9, 3.11, Corollary 3.2, Theorems 3.4, 3.6, 3.13, Proposition 3.7, Definition 3.5); printed pp. 11-24

contents.name: Definition 2.1 (globally hyperbolic development of initial data)
contents.support: Absorbed into clause (a) of the definition, which states time orientation, embedding, field equations and the Cauchy property without global hyperbolicity being part of the definition.

contents.name: Definition 2.2 (extension of a globally hyperbolic development)
contents.support: Absorbed into clause (c): the source requires an isometric embedding onto an open subset; the development-embedding definition records exactly this, and Lemmas 3.1/3.3 replace the source hypothesis by the data-fixing form.

contents.name: Remark 2.5 (diffeomorphism invariance of the field equations)
contents.support: The invariance is absorbed into the data-fixing isometry definition: field equations are transported along the isometry, so isometric developments carry the same solution class.

contents.name: Theorem 2.6 (existence of a GHD and of a common GHD of two GHDs)
contents.support: The existence of a development is supplied in the batch by the local-development inputs; the gluing of two developments into one development is proved in lem-gr-development-pair-gluing, whose quotient is a development containing both.

contents.name: Theorem 2.7 (global uniqueness: one GHD extends two given ones)
contents.support: Proved in the form that the glued quotient of two developments contains both by data-fixing development embeddings; this is the source Theorem 2.7 in the smooth setting of the batch.

contents.name: Theorem 2.8 (existence of the MGHD; uniqueness up to isometry)
contents.support: Proved as the maximality and uniqueness of the universal development, split into the universal-development construction and the second-countability lemma.

contents.name: Lemma 3.1 (an isometric immersion of a connected Lorentzian manifold is determined by value and differential at one point)
contents.support: Proved as clause (a) with the open-and-closed agreement-set argument.

contents.name: Corollary 3.2 (two time-orientation preserving isometric immersions agreeing on the Cauchy surface agree)
contents.support: Absorbed into clauses (b)-(c): agreement on the surface is upgraded to equality of differentials and then to rigidity.

contents.name: Lemma 3.3 (an isometric immersion with a diffeomorphism on the Cauchy surface is an embedding)
contents.support: Proved as clauses (a)-(b) including the injectivity argument via maximal geodesics.

contents.name: Theorem 3.4 (existence of the MCGHD)
contents.support: Proved as the union of all common subdevelopments with the patched map.

contents.name: Definition 3.5 (corresponding boundary points)
contents.support: Proved as clause (c) of the definition.

contents.name: Theorem 3.6 (corresponding boundary points yield a strictly larger common development)
contents.support: Proved in contrapositive form: a maximal common development has no corresponding boundary points.

contents.name: Proposition 3.7 (equivalent characterizations of corresponding boundary points)
contents.support: Proved as the structural form of the corresponding set used in the batch.

contents.name: Lemma 3.8 (the set C is open in the boundary and the embedding extends smoothly)
contents.support: Proved with the corrections recorded in the item: no isometry on the part outside the closure, and connection compatibility in place of an isometry claim.

contents.name: Lemma 3.9 (existence of an exposed point with J^-(p) cap dU cap J^+(Sigma) = {p})
contents.support: Proved as the exposed-boundary-point lemma used to start the restart analysis.

contents.name: Lemma 3.11 (the spacelike level hypersurface through the exposed point)
contents.support: Proved as the spacelike-restart-hypersurface lemma, including the flow-tube and endpoint analysis.

contents.name: Theorem 3.13 (the MCGHD has no corresponding boundary points)
contents.support: Proved as the main theorem of the corresponding-boundary route.

contents.name: Sections 1.3-1.5 (Choquet-Bruhat-Geroch Zorn route and schematic comparison)
contents.reason: The batch follows the Zorn-free dezornification route of the source; the historical Zorn-lemma proof and the schematic comparison of proofs are expository and add no statement used by any item.

sources.title: P. T. Chrusciel, Elements of causality theory, arXiv:1110.6706 (2011), lecture notes
sources.locator: Chapter 2, Sections 2.1-2.3 (causality background, geodesic convexity) and Sections 2.9-2.10 (domains of dependence and their globally hyperbolic interiors); printed pp. 8-13 and 45-52

contents.name: Proposition 2.2.2 (integral curves of the gradient of a function of constant norm are geodesics)
contents.support: Absorbed into the flow-line/geodesy clause of the time-separation lemma, where the flow of grad tau is identified with maximizer geodesics.

contents.name: Proposition 2.2.3 (normal coordinate rays are affinely parameterized geodesics)
contents.support: Absorbed into the normal-coordinate/exponential-map input used for local isometry rigidity.

contents.name: Proposition 2.2.6 (every short geodesic segment with endpoints in a ball stays in the ball)
contents.support: Absorbed into the convex-normal-neighbourhood supplier of the batch; no separate batch item is required.

contents.name: Definition 2.2.7 (elementary region: normal-coordinate ball with compact closure and timelike gradient and time coordinate)
contents.support: Absorbed into the causal-convexity argument, where elementary regions supply the local causal convexity used in the convexity lemma.

contents.name: Corollary 2.9.8 (one-sided neighbourhood property in the domain of dependence)
contents.support: Absorbed into the domain-of-dependence structure of the partial-Cauchy-development lemma.

contents.name: Theorem 2.9.9 (the interior of a domain of dependence is globally hyperbolic)
contents.support: The batch proves the corresponding statements for closed, acausal, edgeless hypersurfaces: D(S) is open and causally convex and S is a Cauchy set of D(S).

contents.name: Lemma 2.9.11 (every inextendible causal curve through an interior point of D(S) meets S)
contents.support: Absorbed into the Cauchy-set clause of the partial-Cauchy-development lemma.

contents.name: Chapter 1 (introductory causality background)
contents.reason: Introductory material on Lorentzian manifolds and causality conventions is already covered by the published framework page gr-framework-and-geometry; repeating it here would duplicate published content.

sources.title: E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3, open access full text
sources.locator: Chapter 2 (normal neighbourhoods, position vector and Gauss lemma: Definition 2.3, Theorems 2.4-2.6, Proposition 2.84) and Chapter 3 (domains of dependence and Cauchy horizons: Lemma 3.8, Propositions 3.10 and 3.43, Corollaries 3.36 and 3.47); printed pp. 26-27, 59-60 and 84-99

contents.name: Definition 2.3 (convex normal and strictly convex normal neighbourhoods)
contents.support: Absorbed into the strictly-convex-neighbourhood fact used to prove the rigidity lemma.

contents.name: Theorem 2.4 (existence of strictly convex normal neighbourhoods)
contents.support: Absorbed into the published supplier thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods used throughout the batch.

contents.name: Theorem 2.6 (Gauss' lemma and the squared distance function)
contents.support: Absorbed into the position-vector differential supplier of the batch.

contents.name: Proposition 2.84 (elementary properties of future and past sets)
contents.support: Absorbed into the Cauchy-set topology and graph lemma of the framework.

contents.name: Proposition 3.10 (for closed S the causal and timelike domains of dependence agree)
contents.support: Quoted verbatim in step 1.1 of the item and used to obtain openness of D(S) around points outside S.

contents.name: Lemma 3.8 (for achronal S, D-tilde^+ cap D-tilde^- equals D^+ cap D^- equals S)
contents.support: Quoted verbatim in step 1.1 of the item and used to separate the chronological sides.

contents.name: Corollary 3.36 (for a partial Cauchy hypersurface D(S) cap H(S) is empty, so D(S) is open)
contents.support: Quoted verbatim in step 1.1 of the item; this is the openness input for the domain of dependence.

contents.name: Proposition 3.43 (the chronological interiors of D(S), D^+(S), D^-(S) are causally convex)
contents.support: Quoted verbatim in step 1.1 of the item; this is clause (b) of the partial-Cauchy-development lemma.

contents.name: Corollary 3.47 (existence of a maximizing causal geodesic from S to an interior point)
contents.support: Absorbed into the maximizer-existence clause of the time-separation lemma.

contents.name: Chapters 4-6 (causal hierarchy, singularity theorems, topology)
contents.reason: The higher causality hierarchy, singularity theorems and topological results of the survey are not used anywhere in this batch; the batch needs only the normal-neighbourhood and domain-of-dependence core of Chapters 2-3.
